entries.name: Sunlit Architectural Miniature
entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one full detailed GeoMarketeer neighborhood illustration, exploring a completely FRESH visual language and palette, not another blue-coded version.
Target 1536 x 1024 landscape, 3:2 aspect ratio. One artwork, not a comparison sheet, not UI, not a storyboard, not a website. No headings, handwritten labels, callout lines, blue dashed opening-view guide, metrics, big map pins, or data panels. Only a small transit sign at underground metro may remain.
The attached image is the LOCKED GEOGRAPHIC COMPOSITION ONLY. Its pencil style, blue accents, annotation labels and colors are NOT the desired style. Preserve the elevated isometric view, full neighborhood crop, density and relative massing: five residential towers grouped around shared garden back LEFT, medium-height office cluster upper RIGHT, underground metro stairwell and small canopy middle RIGHT beside a busy pedestrian area, detached one-storey retail building and parking center, the existing cafe row at the BOTTOM FOREGROUND, side buildings, street network, crossings, planting, cars, scooters and people as positioned. No new landmark, redesigned road plan or cropped-off towers. Maintain architectural proportions and a readable hierarchy, faithful overall neighborhood arrangement. No physical layout redesign.
STORY: Sid's prospective premises is the TWO-STOREY UNIT BETWEEN OPERATING CAFES IN THE BOTTOM FOREGROUND ROW, originally blue-awning unit in the source. It is vacant, has bare interior and NO cafe terrace tables or seated customers directly in front of its own frontage. Adjacent cafes are operating with seated customers. Passing pedestrians remain along the shared pavement. The detached central building is a generic local shop, not the candidate site. No successful new cafe or relocation is depicted.
Critical palette reset: no monochrome blue, no periwinkle city, no cobalt outlines, no blue trees, no uniformly blue glazing. Treat every surface according to the new direction. The color style must be visibly different at a glance from a blue-white tech illustration.

DIRECTION NAME: SUNLIT ARCHITECTURAL MINIATURE.
A high-end physical architectural diorama photographed under warm late-afternoon sunlight, with convincing material variety, beautiful soft cast shadows and tactile solid forms. Cream and warm off-white plaster residential towers, subtle terracotta and weathered brick accents, charcoal metalwork, warm gray concrete, muted bronze/smoky neutral glass office facades. Realistic richly varied olive/sage/deep-green tree canopies and shrubs, not pastel blue vegetation. Streets dark warm-gray asphalt with white crossing paint, sidewalks sandy stone, modest warm-toned cars, realistic terracotta and ochre cafe awnings. Candidate's awning a muted rust red, recognizable among beige and olive neighboring awnings. Tiny carefully modeled people with natural varied clothing colors. Preserve source architecture and floor counts: flat roofs remain flat, no arbitrary pitched roofs. Facades, balcony rails and windows crisp and intentional, no technical contour ink. No plastic toy gloss, no porcelain blue, no papercraft surfaces, no cartoon oversized heads. Entire diorama sharply readable, minimal depth of field, white-to-warm-ivory seamless background. Cohesive warm natural materials, grown-up architectural model photography, inviting urban life. This should look materially and atmospherically different from the previous cold white-blue miniature.

DIRECTION NAME: PAINTED EVERYDAY CITY.
A sophisticated HAND-PAINTED EDITORIAL GOUACHE illustration of the locked neighborhood, as commissioned for a thoughtful contemporary architecture/culture magazine. This is a flat, expressive drawn image, NOT a 3D render or physical scale model. Warm ivory paper, dusty apricot and pale peach building facades, burnt-sienna and rose awnings, deep forest-green and olive foliage, warm charcoal roads and fine dark-brown selective ink accents. Small accents of mustard and muted burgundy in people and vehicles. No blue-coded palette. Facades are intentional flat painted planes with visible matte brush texture, slightly irregular confident edges, restrained pigment variation, and a few crisp dry-brush architectural details. Use one main contour where needed, not dense wireframe grids. Render trees as broad layered brush masses rather than individual leaves or geometric paper cutouts. Windows and balconies are rhythmical edited painted marks, retain counts/massing without technical line overload. People have expressive gestural poses and varied clothes; busy cafe terraces feel lively and human, not generic miniature mannequins. Cars are charming but anatomically plausible simplified painted shapes. Preserve elevated isometric street geometry and building positions from reference, but express them through painterly 2D illustration. No photorealistic material, no smooth 3D gradients, no dramatic cinematic lens, no infantile cartoon faces, no rough storyboard annotations. Detailed enough to zoom into the cafe lane, but deliberately edited areas of detail and quiet flat color balance the dense composition. All map visible on ivory paper. Candidate unit in foreground row has muted burgundy awning, empty glazing and empty frontage, beside lively neighbors. No text besides a small M transit sign.

DIRECTION NAME: BOLD URBAN SCREENPRINT.
Make a striking contemporary GRAPHIC SCREENPRINT EDITORIAL MAP illustration. Absolutely FLAT 2D ink shapes with a limited FOUR-INK palette: warm cream paper, very deep AUBERGINE (not navy) #33233E, vivid persimmon/coral #ED7051, and acid CHARTREUSE #CFDB69. NO blue anywhere, no realistic green trees, no beige architectural rendering, no 3D lighting or gradients, no soft ambient occlusion, no miniature photography, no watercolor. This needs to be visually RADICALLY different from a rendered model: bold positive/negative shapes, confident geometric simplification, subtle risograph ink grain and occasional overprint, carefully aligned architecture. Render the source's isometric building masses as cream and coral filled planar polygons with deep plum shadow faces and simplified window rhythms, NOT wireframe outlines. Draw trees and bushes as bold chartreuse flat scalloped or rounded graphic masses, simple dark trunks. Street planes are deep aubergine with cream crossings and markings, make pedestrian paths legible. Human figures tiny expressive flat silhouettes with coral/cream outfits; scooters, cars, cafe awnings and furniture are purposeful edited graphic shapes. Single-story shop remains centered, empty proposed unit in bottom cafe row has solid coral awning and bare cream glazing; adjacent operating cafe awnings chartreuse/cream with lively terraces. Office windows dark plum bands, residential tower balconies crisp rhythmic cream/coral marks. High contrast but control dark coverage, leave generous cream background around full map. Strict orthographic isometric perspective faithful to attached locked map, retain all district positions, towers and cafe row, no framing text, no poster title. Detailed yet graphic and economical: show neighborhood density with architectural rhythm, do not enumerate every tiny leaf/window. Gallery-quality designed editorial illustration for an experienced UX designer's portfolio, adult and confident, never a generic game map, clipart collection or childish toy city.
